expected_false_negative.check: D-EXTRACT-01 (image-locked facts, the check designed for exactly this)
expected_false_negative.why: Unreachable for one reason only: D-EXTRACT-01 needs a PROBE observation to establish that a fact a user would ask for is missing from the page text, and lib/site_observer/probe.py::detect_capability() returns {'available': False, 'reason': 'MODEL_UNAVAILABLE'} unconditionally, so PROBE observations never exist through the real pipeline. Without it there is no evidence that the image carries a fact the text omits, and asserting one would be fabrication. The audit now reports this explicitly: run_audit emits an X-COV-01 coverage entry with reason UNAVAILABLE_INSTRUMENT naming D-EXTRACT-01, so the check reads as not-evaluable rather than as evaluated-and-passed. CORRECTION (supersedes an earlier note here): a previous version of this field claimed a second, more fundamental cause -- that run_audit.py::_invoke_detectors() never called detect_render()/detect_extract(). That orchestrator gap was real when written and has since been fixed; _invoke_detectors() calls both today. Other D-EXTRACT checks do run end to end (D-EXTRACT-02 and D-EXTRACT-04 fire from full run_audit() passes on other fixtures). The claim of an orchestrator bug is withdrawn; only the probe gap remains.

notes: The clearest single demonstration that the marketplace's stated probe-driven-extractability differentiator is not wired into the shipped pipeline -- and that even if it were, the detector that would use it is itself never invoked.
